note: Both are methods answering the same question: find a basis for the span of given vectors. But they are genuinely different procedures. Apostol's Gram-Schmidt orthogonalizes by subtracting projections onto earlier vectors to produce an ORTHOGONAL basis; Strang's method uses row-reduction/elimination (nonzero rows of R, or pivot columns of A) to produce an arbitrary basis. Producing an orthogonal basis is a special (stronger) case of producing a basis, so the concrete elimination task s505 is the more general one. Types match: both are method, so no type-flip.
Explicit Gram-Schmidt formulas y_{r+1}=x_{r+1}-sum((x,y_i)/(y_i,y_i))y_i (notation). The concrete elimination method gives no such orthogonalization formula. No concrete counterpart.

Orthogonalization Theorem 15.13: an abstract EXISTENCE theorem asserting an orthogonal sequence y_k exists with orthogonality, span-preservation, and uniqueness. The concrete text states no existence theorem at all; it only gives a computational procedure. This theorem-with-no-concrete-counterpart is a key finding: abstract asserts existence, concrete only computes.
Existence theorem 15.14: every finite-dimensional Euclidean space has an orthonormal basis. No concrete existence-theorem counterpart; concrete text only computes a basis.

Existence claim: every finite-dimensional Euclidean space has an orthogonal basis (the Gram-Schmidt output is an orthogonal basis for the same space). Concrete text gives no existence theorem, only a procedure. No counterpart.

Property (b): span preservation L(y_1..y_k)=L(x_1..x_k), stated as a property of the abstract orthogonalization theorem. The concrete elimination implicitly preserves the span but states no such preservation claim as a standalone item. No direct counterpart.
Property (c): uniqueness of the orthogonalized sequence except for scalar factors. No concrete counterpart.
Concept: projection of x along y, ((x,y)/(y,y))y, the building block Gram-Schmidt subtracts. The concrete elimination procedure uses no projections. No counterpart.
Normalized Legendre polynomials phi_n=y_n/||y_n||: a concrete example output of orthogonalization. No counterpart in Strang's elimination procedure.
Legendre polynomials from applying orthogonalization to x_n(t)=t^n under the integral inner product. Concrete example; no counterpart.
Example 2: best polynomial approximation f_n of a continuous function via projection onto the Legendre span. No counterpart in Strang's elimination procedure.
